Subject: GCP co-sell: joint account orchestration & priority mapping — Bluefin Analytics

Hi Daniel / Susan —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Bluefin's usage profile and upcoming data-platform expansion look like a strong fit for a GCP co-sell path. I put together a lightweight priority map to identify the accounts and motions we should align on for listing + joint pursuit.

Attached: redwood-gcp-field-priority-map.xlsx (high-level account priorities, recommended owner, suggested SKU mapping).

Quick asks to get this moving: 
- Daniel: can you confirm the three Bluefin business units that should be part of the joint motion (platform, analytics, procurement)?
- Susan/GCP PM: can you block 45 mins next week for a handshake to align incentives and confirm marketplace listing ownership?
- Marissa / Ben (cc): we'll need swift readiness on the listing artifact side — Marissa, can your team own the listing checklist? Ben, can you validate technical integration and any MLP/POC requirements?

Goal: agree on a priority map, assign owners, and target a marketplace listing submission window (tentatively: 10/15).

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0126

Vivek —

Appreciate the doc and the clear asks. Bluefin confirms the three business units to include are: Platform Engineering, Data Science Ops, and Strategic Procurement. I'll loop in our lead for Platform (cc'd below in a follow-up) for technical details.

A couple of clarifying points before the handshake: 
- Platform Engineering wants to understand expected integration effort (tokens, data flow, ingress controls).
- Procurement needs a rough timeline and any standard SOW/cost commitments for the POC.

We can do a handshake with Susan next Tue (9/7) afternoon PT. Please share any internal checklist or marketplace artifacts we should review before then.

Best,
Daniel Park
Head of Cloud Partnerships, Bluefin Analytics

Thanks Daniel —

Uploading a short packet to frame the handshake: 
- bluefin-account-snapshot.pdf (high-level org map + purchase cadence)
- gcp-listing-checklist.docx (checklist we use for all marketplace submissions: SKU, billing model, regional availability, security attestations)

Marissa: can you review the checklist and call out any blockers for a 10/15 listing window? If not, propose a mitigation plan.
Ben: the Platform team will want to know whether we require any custom connector or if standard REST/KV > GCS integration is sufficient. If you can give a 1-pager on integration risk/effort, we'll share with Platform Engineering.

Susan: 9/7 2:30pm PT works for us for a 45-minute handshake. Can you confirm and send calendar invite with a GCP PM on the line?

Thanks —
Vivek

Vivek / Ben —

I reviewed the checklist. High-level notes: 
- SKU definition: need SKU owner and pricing band from finance; I'll request a provisional SKU but we should expect iteration.
- Compliance: Bluefin will need to complete a short security attestation; procurement may push for SOC 2 evidence — flagging to Security for a quick pull of our public artifacts.
- Documentation: I'll own the listing copy and the end-to-end customer flow diagrams. ETA: drafts by 9/10.

Ben, can you prepare the 1-pager on integration effort by EOD 9/8? I'll sync that to Platform Engineering. Also tagging Priyom (cc'd) for any automation tasks on our side (billing test accounts, sandbox linking).

Vivek / Daniel —

Quick technical summary for Platform Engineering: 
- Integration path: standard REST endpoints + optional GCS connector. No custom kernel or data residency changes required for the POC.
- Effort estimate: 2 engineer-weeks to wire end-to-end (sandbox creds, ingress whitelisting, basic telemetry).
- Risk: billing reconciliation with GCP marketplace requires mapping our SKU to Bluefin's purchase flow; procurement should expect a short coordination window (1 week).

Attaching: gcp-integration-1pager.pdf

If this looks good, Daniel, procurement can propose a provisional SOW and we can start the POC once access is provisioned.
